# SedCoreTool

[![Tests](https://github.com/SantiCa/SedCoreTool/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/SantiCa/SedCoreTool/actions/workflows/tests.yml)
[![License: GPL-3.0-or-later](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--3.0--or--later-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

**SedCoreTool** (*Sediment Core Tool*) quantifies bioturbation and ichnotaxa in sediment-core images and combines them
with any other down-core record — geochemistry, foraminifera, TOC, colour, magnetic susceptibility — and with
described intervals, on a common depth or age axis.

It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, or in a web browser, and keeps all data on the user's computer. A Python package
with the same analysis definitions is available for scripting and batch processing.

> **Status:** version 0.x, in active development. Version 1.0 will be released when the program is considered
> complete. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).

---

## Features

- **Bioturbation from core images.** Percentage of bioturbated area and of each ichnotaxon per depth interval, with
  the Bioturbation Index (BI) and the ichnofabric index (ii) derived automatically or entered manually.
- **High-resolution TIFF.** Import tiled or stripped TIFF and BigTIFF in supported grayscale or RGB formats.
  Enhancement uses native 16-bit samples for levels and gamma, and the project keeps the original image.
  See [working resolution and TIFF limits](docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md#61-working-resolution).
- **Assisted segmentation.** Image enhancement (including published protocols), automatic detection of candidate
  traces, drawing and editing tools, an exclusion layer for cracks, voids and samples, and optional learned
  segmentation (U-Net).
- **Ichnotaxa identification.** A classifier learns from the traces you label and suggests the ichnotaxon of the
  rest, rejecting shapes unlike any example; you review every suggestion.
- **Core column.** All sections of a core on one depth or age axis, with images, traces, indices and external records.
- **Multiproxy analysis.** Numerical records and described intervals of many cores; user-defined classifiers
  (random forest, neural network, k-nearest neighbours, naive Bayes, k-means) validated by leaving whole cores out;
  maps by age window with several interpolation methods and projections.
- **Publication figures.** Core column, ichnotaxa distribution, representative traces, core sections and core
  location maps, as SVG, PNG or JPEG, with editable colours, axes and labels.
  Whole-core, core-column and ichnotaxa distribution plots can combine separate, stacked or overlaid abundances,
  symmetric curves, adjustable opacity, percentage labels and symbols or names at manual presence marks.
- **Reproducible and shareable.** Every parameter is stored in the project together with the original images;
  exported tables record the version and settings used. Projects can be shared as a single file or through a shared
  folder, with comments.

## Installation

### The program

Download the installer for your system from the [latest release](../../releases/latest):

| System | File |
|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `SedCoreTool-V0.<n>-windows-setup.exe`, or `…-windows-portable.exe` (no installation) |
| macOS 13 or later (Intel and Apple Silicon) | `SedCoreTool-V0.<n>-mac-universal.dmg` |
| Linux (x64) | `SedCoreTool-V0.<n>-linux-x86_64.AppImage` or `…-linux-amd64.deb` |
| Any system, in a browser | `SedCoreTool_V0.<n>.html` — a single file that opens with a double click, offline |

The installers are not code-signed: on Windows choose *More info → Run anyway* if SmartScreen appears; on macOS open
the program the first time with right-click → *Open*. To update, install the new version over the old one; projects
are kept. Each release includes `SHA256SUMS.txt` and `RELEASE_MANIFEST.json` to verify the downloads.

The program can also be run from a copy of this repository: start a local server (`python3 -m http.server`) and
open `http://localhost:8000/app/`.

### The Python package

```bash
pip install "sedcoretool @ git+https://github.com/SantiCa/SedCoreTool.git"
# optional extras: excel (Excel export), plot (matplotlib), unet (U-Net training)
pip install "sedcoretool[excel,plot] @ git+https://github.com/SantiCa/SedCoreTool.git"
```

Requires Python 3.10 or later. The package is not on PyPI yet.

## Which part do I need?

| | **The program** | **The Python package `sedcoretool`** |
|---|---|---|
| Starts from | Your core photographs | A **mask**: an image in which bioturbation is already marked (painted, colour-coded per ichnotaxon, exported from the program, or predicted by a U-Net) |
| Does | Everything listed under *Features* | Turns masks into depth or age series of bioturbation %, % per ichnotaxon, BI and ii; trains and evaluates U-Net models |
| For | Anyone analysing cores | Scripted and batch processing |

Most users only need the program. The desktop program uses the Python package behind the scenes when it trains a
U-Net on the computer.

## Quick start (program)

1. **Create a project** and add the images of a core, one per section, with the top and bottom depth of each.
   Large images are reduced for working; the original file is always kept. If an opened section shows a depth
   warning, correct its depth values or unit before using its interval results.
2. **Mark the bioturbation:** enhance the image, detect candidate traces or draw them, and exclude zones that must not
   be counted. Intervals with too few valid pixels are reported as *no data*, never as 0.
   Use **Undo** (Ctrl+Z or ⌘Z) and **Redo** (Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+Shift+Z or ⌘Shift+Z) in the image toolbar.
   Making a new edit after undoing clears Redo. Reopening a project starts with an empty editing history.
3. **Assign ichnotaxa** to some traces; the program suggests the rest, and you accept or correct the suggestions.
4. **Read the results** per interval (thickness in cm): bioturbation %, % per ichnotaxon, BI and ii. Add an age model
   to work in age.
5. **Combine and interpret** in the *Core column*, *Data* and *Multiproxy* modes, and prepare figures in *Figures*.
   In the Data sheet, **Visible rows only (experimental)** limits rendering while you scroll. It is off by default
   and applies only to the current session. Turn it off to return to the current table; CSV exports always include
   every selected row. Active text selections retain their rows until the selection is cleared.
   In Multiproxy, collapse *Numeric variables used* to free space, drag the edge of the name column in
   *Interval families* to resize it, and use *Column order and visibility* in *Curves* to reorder or hide tracks.
   Double-click the name column handle to restore the automatic width. Each multiproxy log
   figure can choose its own proxies. In *Across projects*, select entire projects for an analysis and set
   site map colours and symbols by project or core.
6. **Save and share:** projects are saved automatically on your computer. *Export this project (with images)* creates
   a `.sedcoretool` file that opens on any system; an automatic copy can be kept in a synchronised folder.
   If saving fails, the last complete save is preserved and your pending changes stay open. Use **Retry save**
   before opening another project, or export the current project to keep a separate copy. If the folder copy fails,
   use **Reactivate automatic backup** to retry it.
   A project with an invalid analysis region or broken mask references opens for inspection, with a warning in
   the affected section. Edits are temporary and a project export keeps the original data.

The built-in help and guided tour explain each step. The downloads contain no sample data.

In the **Sections** panel, **Optimised navigation preview** starts enabled and uses a separate thumbnail
cache for the section navigator. Disable it to use the previous renderer for the current session; reloading
enables it again. This display choice is not saved in projects. See the
[promotion checks and limits](docs/benchmarks/M2.2.4.md).

In **Figures**, use **Ichnotaxa in the charts** to choose abundance shapes and occurrences independently.
For names at manually identified positions, select **Names only** and **Manual marks only**; add bars or
symmetric curves and percentage labels as needed. Opacity 100% is opaque. Figure tabs keep their own choices.
The same controls are available in the core-column style panel; presence marks retain their depth or age and
do not supply a measured abundance. See the [figure presentation methods](docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md#2031-ichnotaxon-presentation).

For a **Multiproxy log** figure, select the core, numeric variables and core tracks, then add ichnotaxa with
the same presentation controls. Use **Column order and visibility** to mix taxon, proxy, index and interval
tracks in the desired order. Height, window, widths, scales and colours belong to that figure tab. Reset the
composition to follow the Multiproxy view again; the analysis settings and other figures remain unchanged.
Use the figure's **Vertical axis** and image controls to select depth or age, panels, overlays and excluded
zones independently of Multiproxy and the core column. Age images require the selected core's age model.

**Whole interpreted core** and **Core column** figures also keep their own tracks, records, axes, colours,
widths and image options. Distribution and section figures keep their own style and depth window. Settings
are independent for each figure type and tab; **Restore inherited presentation** removes that type's
presentation override. Existing projects inherit their previous presentation until you edit these controls.

## Quick start (Python package)

```bash
# image with bioturbation painted black; top and bottom of the image at 0 and 500 cm
sedcoretool analyze core.png --top 0 --bottom 500 --units cm --bin-px 100 -o core.csv

# colour-coded mask, e.g. the *_mask.png and *_palette.json exported by the program
sedcoretool analyze core_mask.png --top 0 --bottom 500 --palette palette.json --bin-cm 1 -o core.xlsx

# several sections and cores: list the images, fill in top/bottom, then run them all (CSV, Excel or LAS)
sedcoretool manifest scans/ -o scans/sections.csv
sedcoretool batch scans/sections.csv --palette palette.json --bin-cm 1 -o results.las
```

An exclusion image of the same size (white = excluded: cracks, gaps, samples) can be given with `--exclude`, or as
the `exclude` column of the manifest. The CLI accepts finite `--min-valid` fractions from 0 to 1, inclusive.
Multi-core LAS exports require distinct filenames and unused destinations. If core names collide after
normalisation, rename the cores or export them separately. Use a different output prefix if a destination exists.

```python
from sedcoretool import analyze_mask, load_image, mask_from_palette

mask, names = mask_from_palette(load_image("core_mask.png", "RGB"), {"Zoophycos": "#ff0000", "Chondrites": "#0000ff"})
section = analyze_mask(mask, top=0, bottom=500, units="cm", bin_cm=1, class_names=names)
section.add_age(model_depth=[0, 500], model_age=[0, 40_000])     # optional age model
section.data.to_csv("core.csv", index=False)                     # depth, bioturbation_pct, <class>_pct, BI, ii, age
```

CSV and Excel results escape text that spreadsheet programs could interpret as formulas. Project and U-Net ZIP
imports apply the [project ZIP limits](docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md#231-project-packages-sedcoretool) and [U-Net ZIP limits](docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md#92-training-data-and-training-python-package).
If a project package reports a CRC mismatch, use an intact copy of the package.

Centimetre intervals use the same row boundaries in Python and the application. When updating Python from
V0.120 or earlier, rerun analyses with fractional pixel intervals: corrected half-row boundaries can change
percentages and indices. See the [interval definition](docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md#32-per-interval).

Use lossless formats (PNG, TIFF) for masks. The complete API, command line and U-Net commands are described in the
[technical documentation](docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md#25-the-sedcoretool-python-package).
Python image and mask loading reports an error before decoding if a file exceeds its estimated 768 MiB
[per-load memory budget](docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md#image-loading-budget).
Python analysis accepts integer label IDs from 0 to 255 and up to 255 classes. Use `--exclude-value` to
mark an ignore value in a CLI label mask.

**Learned segmentation (experimental).** A U-Net can be trained on the traces reviewed in the program — from the
desktop program (*Detection → U-Net → Train on this computer…*) or with `sedcoretool unet` — and then used as a
detection method. No model trained on real cores is distributed yet.

Training checks GPU memory and continues on CPU if the accelerator is unavailable or runs out of memory.
Use `sedcoretool unet train DATA OUT --cpu-only` or `train(..., cpu_only=True)` to train on CPU without
probing CUDA or Metal. The `predict` and `evaluate` subcommands also accept `--cpu-only`.

When preparing training data from the command line, choose a new or empty output directory for each preparation.
Preparation assigns portable tile filenames and requires unique core/section identifier pairs. If a duplicate
is reported, correct the identifiers before retrying. Linked paths inside the output folder are refused.
Existing prepared datasets remain usable; keep the same prepared folder when resuming a training run.
While any core is reserved for a final test, the ichnotaxon classifier excludes all library and other-project
examples, whose independence cannot be established for older model files.

## Privacy

Images and data never leave the computer. The program connects to the internet only for optional downloads: map
backgrounds (Esri, GEBCO; only after you allow it, since the map extent is sent), the vision model (Hugging Face) and,
in the browser version, a few libraries. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

| [paper/](paper/) | Software paper (in preparation) |

For reproducible measurements of large-image opening and navigation, see the
[benchmark command, results and limits](docs/benchmarks/M2.2.md). It uses public and deterministic synthetic
projects and verifies edits, saved reloads and every pixel of the exported mask.

## Repository layout

```
app/              the program (HTML and JavaScript ES modules; vendor/ = bundled libraries and fonts)
desktop/          desktop packaging (Electron) for Windows, macOS and Linux
src/sedcoretool/  Python package (src/ichantool/ is an alias for the former name)
tests/            Python, program and end-to-end tests, including the regression against version 2.1
examples/         public example data: IODP U1385I-1H core, idealised core, multiproxy demo, training project
tools/            offline build, version sync, release and synthetic-data scripts
docs/             technical documentation and roadmap
paper/            software paper
legacy/           original version 2.1 (2019), unchanged
```

## History and earlier names

SedCoreTool started in 2019 as **IchAnTool**, a script that turned hand-segmented core images into bioturbation series.
It was renamed **CorAnTool** in 2026 and **SedCoreTool** from version 0.52. Files and code written under the earlier
names keep working: older `.corantool` project packages open, and the Python package can still be imported as
`ichantool`. Version 2.1 is kept unchanged in [`legacy/`](legacy/), archived in Zenodo
([doi:10.5281/zenodo.3518837](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3518837)) and tagged `v2.1` in this repository. The former
repository addresses redirect here.

## Citing

If you use SedCoreTool, please cite the version you used; GitHub shows the citation under *Cite this repository*
(from [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff)).

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Bundled libraries and fonts keep their own licences; see
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

Python developers can opt into the bounded counting experiment with
`SEDCORETOOL_EXPERIMENTAL_COUNTS=1`; unset it to restore the default calculation.
The multi-row experiment meets the measured performance targets on the public and synthetic reference cores
while retaining exact scientific results. It remains opt-in pending default promotion.
See the [measurements and limitations](docs/benchmarks/M3.1.5.md).

# Contributor and AI-assistant guide

This file is the single set of working rules for anyone changing SedCoreTool: human contributors and AI coding
assistants alike (Codex, ChatGPT, Claude and others). Claude reads it through `CLAUDE.md`, which only imports this
file. Keep the rules here and nowhere else.

Owner and maintainer: Santiago Casanova-Arenillas. **Reply to the owner in Spanish**; everything committed to the
repository (code, comments, documentation, commit messages) is written in English.

## 1. What the project is

SedCoreTool quantifies bioturbation and ichnotaxa in sediment-core images and combines them with other down-core
records. It has two parts that share the same analysis definitions:

| Part | Path | Language |
|------|------|----------|
| The program (desktop and browser) | `app/` (web application), `desktop/` (Electron packaging) | JavaScript, no build step |
| The Python package `sedcoretool` | `src/sedcoretool/` (`src/ichantool/` is a compatibility alias) | Python ≥ 3.10 |
| Reference version 2.1 (2019) | `legacy/` | Python 3.7 — never modify |

Start with [README.md](README.md) for users and [docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md](docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md)
for how every part works (§1.4 maps the source files).

## 2. Repository map

```
app/            program: index.html, js/ (ES modules), vendor/ (bundled libraries and fonts)
desktop/        Electron main process, preload, U-Net trainer, build scripts, release notes
src/sedcoretool Python package (analysis, command line, U-Net)
tests/          Python tests, program tests (tests/app), end-to-end tests (tests/e2e), fixtures
examples/       public example data used by tests and by the program when run from the repository
tools/          offline build, version sync, release, vendor update, synthetic data generators
docs/           technical documentation and roadmap
paper/          software paper (JOSS) and its bibliography
legacy/         original version 2.1, unchanged
```

## 3. Setting up and running

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"                 # Python package with test dependencies
pytest -q                               # Python tests
npm test                                # program tests (Node 22; same as: node --test tests/app/*.test.mjs)
npm ci && npm run typecheck             # JavaScript type checks (Node 22)
python3 -m http.server 8765             # then open http://localhost:8765/app/
python3 tools/build_standalone.py       # offline file -> dist/SedCoreTool_V0.<n>.html (dist/ is not committed)
cd desktop && npm ci && npm start       # desktop program; npm run dist builds installers for the current system
npm i --no-save puppeteer-core@23 && node tests/e2e/smoke.mjs   # browser end-to-end test (needs the server above and Chrome)
```

On Windows with a local virtual environment: `python -m venv .venv`, `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e
".[dev]"`, then `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q`. Do not reinstall dependencies if the environment works.

## 4. Rules for code

- **Shared definitions.** Interval limits, percentages, indices and depth mapping must stay identical in Python
  (`src/sedcoretool/`) and JavaScript (`app/js/core.js`); U-Net tiling likewise (`unet/tiling.py`, `app/js/unet.js`).
  Keep the regression test against `legacy/v2.1_console/example_output.csv` passing.
- **Pure modules.** `core.js`, `edit.js`, `imageproc.js`, `learn.js`, `log.js`, `zip.js`, `geo.js`, `interp.js`,
  `locmap.js`, `plot.js`, `sheet.js`, `exportio.js` and `unet.js` must not use the DOM, so they can be tested with
  Node. A new module must be added to `ORDER` in `tools/build_standalone.py`, and top-level names must not clash
  across modules.
- **Compatibility of saved data.** Do not rename the browser storage keys (`ichantool.*`, `corantool.*`), the
  IndexedDB database `ichantool`, the desktop origin `app://corantool` or `window.corantoolDesktop`: users would lose
  their projects. Keep reading project files written as `IchAnTool` or `CorAnTool` and `.corantool` packages. Keep the
  `ichantool` Python alias.
- **Public APIs.** Preserve existing callers. Any approved breaking change needs a documented migration path
  and regression coverage for supported inputs.
- **Measure performance.** Back performance claims with a reproducible benchmark. Record the inputs,
  environment and measured quantities, and use the baseline in [M0.1](docs/roadmap.md#m01-acceptance-criteria)
  when it covers the affected path.
- **Safe I/O.** Handle corrupt, oversized and hostile inputs. Bound resource use when processing untrusted
  files. For filesystem project saves, use a temporary file and atomic replacement where supported. For
  IndexedDB, use transactions. Verify recovery and preservation of the last good save after a failed write.
- **Incremental delivery.** Split broad changes into small, independently testable deliveries. Gate major refactors
  behind a feature flag and keep the current path as the default until the new path passes its acceptance criteria.
  Define how to roll back and when to remove the flag.
- **Dependency discipline.** Prefer existing or standard-library facilities. Justify new dependencies with a
  concrete capability or measured benefit. Before adding a heavy dependency, compare it with the smallest viable
  alternative and document the maintenance, runtime and distribution costs, including offline and desktop use.
- **No private data.** Never commit unpublished data or results of the owner or anyone else. The repository and the
  downloads contain only public example data.
- **Interface texts** go in `app/js/i18n.js`, in Spanish and English.
- **Regression coverage.** Add tests for new features and behaviour changes. Use property-based tests for
  critical invariants where appropriate. When changing scientific code, test numerical equivalence against
  reference results on representative inputs and relevant edge cases. Use exact equality where required and
  define and justify any tolerances before validation. Test an explicitly requested scientific change against
  its new expected results and verify that unaffected outputs remain equivalent. Documentation-only edits
  require no new tests.
- **Documentation.** Update user and technical documentation as required by [section 5](#5-delivering-a-change).

## 5. Delivering a change

Every delivery that changes code, algorithms, defaults or files includes, in the same commit:

1. **Next version number** `V0.<n>` (the latest is the top entry of `CHANGELOG.md`). Set `DELIVERY` in
   `app/js/app.js` and run `python3 tools/sync_version.py`, which writes `0.<n>.0` to `pyproject.toml`,
   `src/sedcoretool/__init__.py`, `CITATION.cff` and `desktop/package.json` (a test checks them).
2. **`CHANGELOG.md`:** a new entry at the top, `## V0.<n> — YYYY-MM-DD`, with short user-facing bullets (what changed
   for the user, not how the work was organised).
3. **`docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md`** if an algorithm, formula, default value, file format or validation result
   changes. Formulas there must match the code exactly. It describes current behaviour for any reader: no history, no
   notes addressed to reviewers.
4. **README** if what users see or do changes.
5. **Tests pass:** `pytest -q`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `python3 tools/sync_version.py --check`, `ruff check src tests tools`;
   run the end-to-end test when the interface or saving changes. Do not re-run them on an unchanged, already verified
   state.
6. **Commit** on `master` with the message `V0.<n>: <summary>` and a short body. Select files explicitly.

Version 1.0 is reserved for when the owner declares the program complete.

**Releases.** `tools/release.sh` checks branch, clean tree, versions and tests, and pushes the tag `V0.<n>`; GitHub
Actions (`.github/workflows/desktop.yml`) then builds Windows, macOS and Linux installers and publishes the Release.
A manual run of *Desktop builds* on `master` with `draft_release` prepares an unpublished draft instead. Before a
release, update `desktop/RELEASE_NOTES.md` (the text of the GitHub Release). Only the owner decides when to publish a
release or a DOI.

## 6. Documentation: what goes where

| Content | Place |
|---------|-------|
| What the software is for, installation, how to use it | `README.md` |
| How each part works: methods, formulas, defaults, file formats, validation | `docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md` |
| What changed in each version | `CHANGELOG.md` |
| Planned work | `docs/roadmap.md` |
| Desktop release notes (text of the GitHub Release) | `desktop/RELEASE_NOTES.md` |
| How to contribute (humans) | `CONTRIBUTING.md` (short; points here) |
| Working rules (humans and AI assistants) | this file |
| Software paper | `paper/` |

Do not repeat content between these files; link instead. Keep the tone factual and professional.

## 7. Working with several people or assistants

- **One editor at a time** on a shared working copy, even for different files: the version number and the changelog
  are shared. Other sessions may read and review.
- **Before editing:** `git fetch origin`, `git status --short --branch`, and `git pull --ff-only` on a clean tree.
  A dirty tree may contain someone else's work: do not stash, reset, clean or discard it, and do not switch branches.
- **Before committing:** fetch again; if someone else delivered meanwhile, rebase or merge and take the next free
  version number. Never force-push or overwrite others' work.
- **Start each iteration** by reading this file and the current [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md). Find the task
  the maintainer authorised, its acceptance criteria and its editor and reviewer, when assigned. The roadmap
  orders the work. Starting a task requires the maintainer's authorisation.
- **Handoff.** Update the roadmap status when handing work over or delivering it. For an unfinished task,
  record the next step or blocker and point to the work under review if available. Mark a task complete once
  its criteria and required checks pass, and link its changelog entry in the same delivery. Sessions rely on
  the repository for handoffs.
- **GitHub handoff.** At each reviewable checkpoint, check whether the next editor or reviewer can retrieve the
  commit from GitHub. If a push is needed, tell the maintainer promptly and provide the branch, commit SHA,
  checks run and next step. If the work is still local and uncommitted, say what needs to be committed first.
  Raise this at the checkpoint so the handoff can happen even if the session ends early. Push only when authorised.
- **Explain each step to the maintainer.** After completing each step, report in Spanish what you did, how you
  checked it and how any implementation works within SedCoreTool as a whole. Describe the affected components and
  how data or control passes between them. Include open work and limitations in the final report.
- **Interpret requests by intent.** If the maintainer gives a broad instruction, infer the smallest concrete scope
  from the request, the repository and the roadmap. Identify the affected workflow and acceptance criteria before
  editing. For performance work, choose the specific path, representative inputs and a reproducible benchmark for
  before-and-after comparison. State material assumptions and ask only when the goal or a consequential choice
  cannot be inferred.
- **One phase at a time.** Split requests that combine independent workstreams, such as UI, GPU, WASM and DuckDB,
  into ordered, independently verifiable phases. Work on the first authorised phase and record the others in the
  roadmap. Do not start unrelated refactors, audits or backlog work. Do not launch sub-agents or automations unless
  asked.
- **Reporting to the owner:** briefly, in Spanish — result, how it was checked, version number, and anything that is
  genuinely pending.

# Security policy

SedCoreTool runs locally: projects and images stay in the browser (IndexedDB) or on the computer (desktop program).
Network requests are made only for optional downloads (map backgrounds from Esri/GEBCO after consent, the DINOv2
vision model from Hugging Face, and libraries from jsDelivr/SheetJS when the bundled copies are missing).

## Supported versions
Only the latest delivery (`V0.<n>`, see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)) receives fixes.

## Reporting a vulnerability
Please do **not** open a public issue. Use GitHub's private reporting (*Security → Report a vulnerability*) or write
to the maintainer (address in `desktop/package.json`). Include the version, the steps to reproduce and, if possible,
a file that triggers the problem. You will get an answer within two weeks.

Files from other people (projects, spreadsheets, images) are parsed in the browser; reports about crafted files that
crash the program or run code are especially welcome.

# Changelog

All notable changes to SedCoreTool are listed here, newest first.

**Versioning.** Each delivery has a number `V0.<n>`, shown in the program and used as the version `0.<n>.0` of the
program, the Python package and the desktop installers. Version 1.0 will be released when the program is considered
complete. Before 5 November 2026, development builds were numbered V1–V33; V33 became V0.1.

Technical details of every method are in [docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md](docs/TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md).

---

## V0.123 — 2026-11-11

- Improve the opt-in Python counting experiment with bounded multi-row histograms; reduce median API time by about 60% on the public reference core and 30% on the synthetic core in an alternating comparison, with less than 1% higher median worker peak memory.
- Preserve exact scientific results and retain the established calculation as the default; no additional dependencies are required.

## V0.122 — 2026-11-11

- Add an opt-in bounded Python counting experiment with exact reference results; retain the established default because the synthetic workload misses the performance target.
- Publish baseline and experimental measurements on the public and synthetic cores.

## V0.121 — 2026-11-11

- Align Python's centimetre-to-row conversion with the application so fractional intervals use identical row boundaries and indices, with matching percentages within the documented numerical tolerance.
- Verify public and synthetic reference cores at 2 and 1.37 cm, half-row boundaries and neighbouring floating-point values, while preserving the historical regression and explicit pixel intervals.

## V0.120 — 2026-11-10

- Publish reproducible interval-analysis profiles on the public and synthetic reference cores, distinguishing fresh pixel counts from reused browser counts and measuring the public Python API.
- Document a fractional-interval boundary disagreement between Python and JavaScript, including its effect on percentages and indices; retain the existing analysis while recording the correction needed before optimisation.

## V0.119 — 2026-11-10

- Enable the optimised navigation preview at startup, with a session control to restore the previous renderer.
- Keep older projects, exported figures and scientific results compatible, and use the existing renderer for unsupported preview dimensions or invalid analysis regions.

## V0.118 — 2026-11-10

- Add an optional, session-only navigation-preview experiment with exact display pixels and a bounded thumbnail cache. Keep the current navigation renderer as the default.
- Reduce first-visit navigation time by 33.7% on the measured 122.9-million-pixel synthetic core, with 4.8% higher median whole-trial peak memory; publish the matched comparison and correctness checks.

## V0.117 — 2026-11-10

- Add reproducible large-image diagnostics for project opening, section navigation, zoom/pan, cache residency and memory, with exact edit/reload and full-resolution mask-export checks.
- Publish measurements on public and synthetic cores, identifying navigation-thumbnail preparation as the next optimisation target.

## V0.116 — 2026-11-10

- Fix creating or importing the first project in an empty library when startup preferences have marked the uninitialised workspace as changed. Keep failed-save protection for existing projects.

## V0.115 — 2026-11-10

- Choose a multiproxy figure's own depth/age axis and image treatment without changing the analysis view. Map age image panels and classification bands through the selected core's depth–age relation.
- Preserve inherited presentation and custom column labels in existing projects, save independent settings with figure tabs, and restore inherited presentation per figure type.

## V0.114 — 2026-11-10

# SedCoreTool — Technical documentation

This document explains how SedCoreTool works: what each part does, the formulas it uses and its default values,
exactly as they are in the code. Each section names the file (and usually the function) where the method is
implemented, written as `file::function`, so that every statement can be checked against the source. Where a
choice needs a reason, or a method has limits that affect how results should be read, the explanation is given in
the same place.

The document describes the current version; the history of changes is in [`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md).

# Part I — Overview

## 1. What SedCoreTool is: the program and the Python package

SedCoreTool (*Sediment Core Tool*) quantifies bioturbation and ichnotaxa in images of sediment cores and combines
them with any other down-core record (geochemistry, micropalaeontology, TOC, colour, magnetic susceptibility…) and
with described intervals (lithology, events…). It has two parts that share the same analysis definitions:

| Part | What it is | Who it is for | Code |
|------|-----------|---------------|------|
| **The program** | An interactive application with windows, tools and figures. It is the same code whether it runs as the **desktop program** (Windows, macOS, Linux) or in a **web browser**. | Anyone analysing cores: image work, interpretation, multiproxy analysis, figures | `app/` (JavaScript), packaged by `desktop/` |
| **The Python package `sedcoretool`** | A library and a command (`sedcoretool`) without a graphical interface | Users who write scripts or process many images, and the U-Net training | `src/sedcoretool/` (Python) |
| Reference version 2.1 | The original 2019 script (IchAnTool v2.1), kept unchanged | Regression tests | `legacy/` |

### 1.1 The program

The program is a web application written in JavaScript (ES modules, no build step). It never sends images or data
to a server: everything is computed on the user's computer. It can be used in three equivalent ways:

- **Desktop program** — installers for Windows, macOS and Linux (§26). It runs the same `app/` code in its own
  window (Electron), with more memory, its data stored in a folder on disk, and the option to train U-Net models
  on the computer's graphics card.
- **Offline single file** — `SedCoreTool_V0.<n>.html`, one HTML file with all the code inside, which opens with a
  double click in Chrome, Edge or Firefox (§27).
- **From a copy of the repository** — served by any local web server (`python3 -m http.server`, then open
  `http://localhost:8000/app/`). This is how it is developed and tested.

The program has five working modes, chosen at the top of the window: **Bioturbation** (image work, §6–§14),
**Core column** (§15–§16), **Data** (§17), **Multiproxy** (§18–§19) and **Figures** (§20). The start screen
(**Projects**, **Across projects**) manages projects (§21–§23).

### 1.2 The Python package

`sedcoretool` is installed with `pip` (§25). It does **not** have the program's image tools: it does not enhance,
detect, edit or classify traces. It starts from a **mask** — an image in which bioturbation has already been
marked, either painted on the photograph (the original 2019 workflow), colour-coded per ichnotaxon, exported
from the program, or predicted by a U-Net — and turns it into depth (or age) series of bioturbation percentage,
per-ichnotaxon percentage and BI/ii indices. It also contains the whole U-Net workflow (prepare, train, evaluate,
predict), which the desktop program calls when the user trains a model (§9).

| Task | Program | Python package |
|------|:-------:|:--------------:|
| Bioturbation %, per-class %, BI, ii, depth and age per interval | ✓ | ✓ (same definitions) |
| Image enhancement, automatic detection, drawing and editing traces | ✓ | — |
| Exclusion layer (cracks, gaps, samples) | ✓ (drawn) | ✓ (exclusion image or mask value) |
| Identifying ichnotaxa (k-NN, Random Forest, Bayes, vision features) | ✓ | — |
| U-Net: run a trained model | ✓ | ✓ |
| U-Net: prepare data, train, evaluate | desktop program (it calls the Python package) | ✓ |
| Core column, external records, Data tab, multiproxy analysis, maps, figures | ✓ | — |
| Batch processing from scripts and the command line, multi-section cores, LAS export | — | ✓ |

The analysis definitions shared by both — interval limits, percentages, indices, depth mapping and the U-Net
tiling — are implemented twice (`src/sedcoretool/` and `app/js/core.js`, `app/js/unet.js`) and the tests check that
both give identical numbers (§31).

### 1.3 Common workflow

```
core image
   → (enhancement)                  program only; changes what is seen and detected, not the calculation
   → label mask                     each pixel: 0 = matrix, n = object or class
   → percentage per pixel row
   → intervals of a set thickness   centre depth, %, % per class
   → BI and ii indices
   → (age)                          interpolation of the age model
   → CSV / Excel / PNG / project
```

On top of the mask, the program keeps a layer of **objects** (traces): each object is a connected set of pixels
with an identifier, a class and shape and colour descriptors. Objects are what the user edits and what the
ichnotaxa classifier learns from.

### 1.4 Source code map

Program (`app/js/`). The modules marked "pure" do not use the browser (no DOM) and are tested with Node.

| File | Content | Pure |
|------|---------|:----:|
| `core.js` | Intervals, indices, age model, CSV, RLE encoding, overlapping-trace stacks | ✓ |
| `imageproc.js` | Enhancement, detection, connected components, magic wand, lasso, descriptors, rotation, downsampling | ✓ |
| `edit.js` | Editing algorithms: scissors, merging, undo records, project migration | ✓ |
| `learn.js` | Ichnotaxa classifier (k-NN with novelty rejection; Random Forest and Bayes wrappers), evaluation, final-test metrics | ✓ |
| `log.js` | Core column: table parsing, axes, ticks, SVG and CSV of a window, distribution figure | ✓ |
| `geo.js` | Multiproxy: samples, interval layers, labels, Random Forest, k-NN, Bayes, neural network, k-means, cross-validation, maps | ✓ |
| `interp.js` | Gridding of scattered values for maps (inverse distance, triangulation, splines, kriging…) and map projections | ✓ |
| `locmap.js` | Core location map: coordinate reference systems, frame, grid, scale | ✓ |
| `plot.js` | Plots of the Data tab (stratigraphic log, XY, fits) | ✓ |
| `sheet.js` | Formulas of the Data tab (own parser, no `eval`) | ✓ |
| `exportio.js` | Tables written to files and records read from tables | ✓ |
| `zip.js` | Minimal ZIP writer and reader for project packages | ✓ |
| `unet.js` | U-Net tiling, normalisation, blending and resampling (same rules as the Python package) | ✓ |
| `vision.js` | Pre-trained vision model (DINOv2): input window and embedding | partly |
| `worker.js` | Background worker that runs enhancement and detection off the interface thread | — |
| `storage.js` | Project library in IndexedDB | — |
| `state.js` | Shared program state (`S`) and small helpers used by the interface modules | — |
| `columns.js` | Composite log of a core: column view, records, order and visibility of chart columns | — |
| `navpreview.js` | Navigation-only photo/mask reduction and bounded preview ownership | ✓ |
| `figview.js` | Serializable figure presentation, inherited defaults and independent overrides | ✓ |
| `panels.js` | Resizable and collapsible side panels, resizable maps | — |
| `datatab.js` | Data tab: all data of the project, Grapher-like plots and the spreadsheet view | — |
| `multiproxy.js` | Multiproxy tool: numeric records, interval layers, classifiers, composite-log readout, manual classification, maps | — |
| `figures.js` | Figures panel: representative traces, interpreted core, logs, sections, range chart, location map | — |
| `app.js` | Interface, tools, drawing, files | — |

The interface modules (`state.js`, `columns.js`, `panels.js`, `datatab.js`, `figures.js`, `multiproxy.js`, `app.js`) import from each other; circular imports are safe because
the imported names are only used inside functions, never while a module is being loaded. A top-level `let` is assigned
only in the module that declares it. Event wiring that must run in a fixed order is wrapped in an `init…()` function
(for example `initMultiproxy`) that `app.js` calls where that code used to run.
| `i18n.js` | Interface texts in Spanish and English | — |

Python package (`src/sedcoretool/`): `io.py` (images and masks), `segmentation.py` (masks from a threshold, a
colour palette or a U-Net), `pipeline.py` (intervals, percentages, indices), `indices.py` (BI and ii schemes),
`depth.py` (depth and age), `export.py` (CSV and Excel), `plotting.py` (matplotlib figure), `cli.py` (command line),
`unet/` (U-Net dataset, training, evaluation, prediction, tiling and metrics).

### 1.5 Names and compatibility

The software started in 2019 as **IchAnTool** and was called **CorAnTool** in 2026 before taking its current name.
Files and data written under the old names keep working:

- The Python package is imported as `sedcoretool` and run as `sedcoretool`. The old name `ichantool` still works,
  as a module (`import ichantool`, `import ichantool.cli`…) and as a command, with a deprecation warning.
- New project files say `app: 'SedCoreTool'`; files with `app: 'CorAnTool'` or `app: 'IchAnTool'` are read as well.
  Shareable project packages use the extension `.sedcoretool`; older `.corantool` packages open too.
- Some internal names keep the old spelling on purpose, because changing them would make previously saved data
  disappear: the browser storage keys (`ichantool.*`, `corantool.author`), the IndexedDB database `ichantool`, the
  vision-model cache `corantool-models`, the desktop page origin `app://corantool` and the desktop bridge
  `window.corantoolDesktop`. The desktop program keeps using an existing `CorAnTool` data folder if the new
  `SedCoreTool` folder does not exist yet.
- Environment variables: `SEDCORETOOL_PYTHON` (also read as `CORANTOOL_PYTHON`), `SEDCORETOOL_TEST_PROFILE`,
  `SEDCORETOOL_VISION_MODEL` and `SEDCORETOOL_NETWORK_SMOKE`.
